The Areopagus, a rocky hill in Athens named after Ares, the Greek god of war (the Roman Mars). The city’s ancient council took its name from it.
Ancient writers, and the Book of Acts, mention altars in Athens dedicated to an unknown god, so that no deity would be left out of the city’s worship.
An old English form of the Hebrew name of God. Devout Jews avoided speaking the name aloud and said “the Lord” instead.
A military tribune was a senior officer in a Roman legion, usually a young man from a wealthy family starting a public career.
The Emperor Tiberius spent his last years on Capri, an island in the Bay of Naples, in a cliff-top palace called the Villa Jovis. He was known for suspicion and kept astrologers around him.
The standard Roman silver coin, about a day’s pay for a labourer.
Not a coin but a large weight of silver or gold, used to count big sums of money.
The harbour town of Athens, a few miles from the city, where ships from across the Mediterranean docked.
The port of Rome, at the mouth of the River Tiber.
Two old cities on or near the coast of southern Palestine, on the road between Egypt and the north.
A small town a few miles south of Jerusalem, remembered in Jewish tradition as the home town of King David.
The valley running along the east side of Jerusalem, between the city walls and the Mount of Olives.

quiz.q: What were Marcellus and Demetrius debating on the road to Piraeus?
o: Whether Zeus or Jehovah deserved more honour
Whether Demetrius should go to Benjamin’s shop
Whether the Jewish Commandments were fair
Whether Aramaic was harder to learn than Greek
quiz.e: Demetrius argued the Commandments were unjust to the poor, since they forbade stealing and coveting but never told the rich to be generous.

quiz.q: Why did Demetrius call the Emperor’s plan to make Marcellus a teacher at Capri a disaster?
o: He feared Marcellus would be poisoned by jealous rivals at court
He thought the work was beneath a Roman officer
He knew Diana would never be allowed to see him
He feared the Robe would be mocked by Tiberius’ soothsayers
quiz.e: Demetrius said Tiberius wanted to hear about the Robe, and he dreaded seeing it reviled by “that loathsome old man” and his crew.

quiz.q: What started the fight between Demetrius and Quintus?
o: Quintus called Marcellus a coward in front of the household
Quintus insulted Theodosia and lunged at Demetrius with a dagger
Quintus ordered Demetrius to be put in chains for a past offence
Quintus struck Dion when he protested about the Tribune’s manners
quiz.e: When Demetrius told Theodosia to go to the house, Quintus drew his dagger; Demetrius disarmed him and beat him senseless with his fists.

quiz.q: What did the Emperor’s letter actually command Marcellus to do?
o: Return to Rome at once and take command of the Capri guard
Sail straight to Capri and begin teaching there
Go to Palestine and learn at first hand about the Galilean
Bring the Galilean’s Robe to Capri for examination
quiz.e: Tiberius wanted to know whether Jesus was thought to be the Messiah; Marcellus was delighted, wanting to know what manner of man he was.

quiz.q: Why did Demetrius leave his manumission scroll behind?
o: He did not want to be free while Marcellus needed him
If caught with it, people might think he was rewarded for the beating
He thought a freed Greek would be hunted more fiercely
Marcellus had forgotten to seal it with his ring
quiz.e: He took the money but laid the scroll on the table, fearing it would look as if Marcellus had rewarded him for punishing Quintus.

quiz.q: How did Demetrius get from Athens to Palestine?
o: He joined a caravan of Greek merchants sailing to Joppa
He stowed away on a grain ship bound for Caesarea
Benjamin paid his passage on a ship to Alexandria
Fulvius hid him on The Vestris and landed him at Gaza
quiz.e: Fulvius hid him in the hold, refused Quintus’ order to put him in irons, and secretly put him ashore in the Bay of Gaza.

quiz.q: What did the fish outline mean, according to Stephanos?
o: It was the sign by which Jesus’ followers knew one another
It marked inns that gave poor travellers shelter
It was the badge of the fishermen of the Galilean lake
It warned travellers that Bedouin raiders were near
quiz.e: Stephanos explained that believers in Jesus, savagely persecuted and meeting in secret, used the fish to identify themselves to one another.

quiz.q: What plan did Demetrius suggest for getting Marcellus into Galilee?
o: Pose as a buyer of Galilean homespun and hire a guide
Travel as a pilgrim going up for the Passover
Join the household of Benyosef as an apprentice weaver
Write to Pilate asking for an escort of legionaries
quiz.e: He proposed that Marcellus pose as a connoisseur of homespun and hire Barsabas Justus as a guide; Benjamin doubted it would work.

chapters.title: Under a Fig Tree
chapters.intro: Background on the Sabbath, the Exodus and the countryside of Samaria and Galilee, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A trick or excuse used to hide what you really want.
Pretending to be someone or something you are not, in order to deceive.
Too eager to please or obey; fawning.
A conversation, often a formal one.
Complaining in a peevish, grumbling way.
A pedlar or market trader, especially a pushy one.
Coaxing or flattering someone into doing what you want.
Apparently or supposedly, though perhaps not really.
To join two pieces of wood by fitting a shaped end into a hole cut in the other.
The Jewish day of rest, from sunset on Friday to sunset on Saturday. The Commandments forbid work on it, and devout Jews kept it strictly.
Yeshayah is the Hebrew form of Isaiah, a prophet of ancient Judah. The book of his prophecies includes many passages Jews read as promises of a coming deliverer.
The story, told in the Book of Exodus, of the Israelites’ escape from slavery in Egypt under Moses. Jews remember it every year at Passover.
One of the patriarchs of Israel, grandson of Abraham. His twelve sons were held to be the ancestors of the twelve tribes.
Son of King David, remembered for his wisdom, his wealth and the splendour of his court.
Early Christians used a simple fish as a secret sign. The Greek word for fish, ichthys, could be read as the first letters of “Jesus Christ, God’s Son, Saviour”.
A village on the far slope of the Mount of Olives, a short walk east of Jerusalem.
The hill country between Judea and Galilee. Jews and Samaritans had long quarrelled over worship and ancestry and often avoided each other.
The northern region of Palestine, a land of farming villages and fishing towns, ruled in this period by Herod Antipas under Rome.
A town in Samaria, near the ancient city of Shechem.
An old well near Sychar that tradition linked with the patriarch Jacob.
A town in Galilee, a few miles north of Nazareth, rebuilt by Herod Antipas.
In the markets of the eastern Mediterranean, prices were never fixed; buyer and seller were expected to argue loudly until they met somewhere in the middle.
Following the commandment against graven images, Jewish art of the period avoided pictures and statues of people and animals.
Winter rains make the hills bloom with wild flowers in early spring; by summer the land turns dry and brown.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus spread word in Jerusalem that he was a buyer of homespun?
o: He posted notices at the Temple gates offering high prices
He overpaid in the bazaars and scolded merchants for low stock
He asked officials at the Insula to send word round the Galilean villages
He hired criers to announce his arrival in the markets
quiz.e: Registering as “M. Lucan”, he bought robes at the first price asked and upbraided the merchants for running short of Galilean textiles.

quiz.q: Who suggested that Justus should act as Marcellus’ guide?
o: Old Benyosef, from his loom
The older of the two brothers
The boy who had been playing with the dog
The young Greek who might be Stephanos
quiz.e: Stephanos turned to Justus and pointed out that he had been intending to go home to Galilee anyway.

quiz.q: Why had Demetrius left Jerusalem before Marcellus arrived?
o: Quintus had recognised him on the street
Benyosef had dismissed him from the shop
He had gone to Galilee to prepare the way
He had been sent away by the Galileans
quiz.e: Fearing the Tribune’s revenge would fall on his friends at Benyosef’s shop, he slipped away before dawn.

quiz.q: What did Stephanos ask of Marcellus at the end of their talk in the inn garden?
o: To carry a letter to Demetrius
To tell no one of their meeting
To let him see the Robe
To keep his nephew out of danger
quiz.e: Stephanos, who had been at the crucifixion, whispered to ask whether Marcellus had the Robe, and was taken to see it.

quiz.q: What first made Justus warm to Marcellus on the road?
o: Marcellus eased a donkey’s cruelly tight bridle
Marcellus offered to double his agreed wages
Marcellus knew the names of the wild flowers
Marcellus asked respectfully about the Sabbath
quiz.e: Seeing him lengthen the bridle that had torn the donkey’s mouth, Justus remarked that he liked animals and began to talk of the carpenter.

quiz.q: According to Justus, what did the carpenter tell the wealthy young nobleman?
o: To build bigger barns and share the harvest
To pay his workers before he paid himself
To go home and keep the Commandments
To give his things away and come along
quiz.e: The young man asked how to get what Jesus had; told to give his things away and follow, he went away depressed, for he could not.

quiz.q: What did Justus refuse to discuss after speaking of his grandson?
o: Why his daughter Rebecca had been widowed
How Jonathan’s crooked foot had come to be well
Where the carpenter friend had gone
Why he kept looking back along the road
quiz.e: When Marcellus asked whether Jonathan’s cure was not unusual, Justus turned away and plainly wished not to be questioned.

quiz.q: What happened at the well near Sychar?
o: A shepherd warned Justus that soldiers were on the road
Justus drew water for a woman and blessed her family
A woman saw them, hurried off and came back with another
Some villagers refused to let a Roman drink from the well
quiz.e: The woman returned with a younger neighbour, pressing Justus with questions he would not answer in front of the Roman.

chapters.title: The Road to Cana
chapters.intro: Background on Galilean villages, the Psalms and Jewish worship, and Roman households, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A Greek measure of distance, about 600 feet (roughly 185 metres); also called a stade.
Saying very little; not inclined to talk.
An old word for someone who drinks too much wine.
Changed in appearance, as if lit up from within.
A loose cloak or mantle worn by Greeks, draped over the body and one shoulder.
A shady garden shelter of trellis covered with vines or climbing plants.
A narrow band worn around the head to hold the hair.
Telling something with gestures and expressions rather than words.
A local Jewish meeting house where people gathered for prayer and to hear the Scriptures read and explained, especially on the Sabbath.
Devout Jews did no work on the Sabbath and travelled only a short distance, so journeys were planned around it.
A book of 150 hymns and prayers in the Hebrew Scriptures, many traditionally linked with King David. They were sung in worship and known by heart.
Hebrew songs were often accompanied by a small lyre or harp, the instrument tradition gives to King David.
Each spring, families from all over the land travelled to Jerusalem to keep the Passover festival at the Temple.
A small village in southern Galilee.
A village in the hills of Galilee, not far from Nazareth.
A city on the western shore of the Lake of Galilee, built by Herod Antipas and named after the Emperor Tiberius. Hot springs nearby drew visitors for their healing baths.
Another name for the Sea of Galilee, a large freshwater lake known for its fishing and its sudden storms.
A garment woven in one piece on the loom, with no seams to sew; a sign of skilled home weaving.
Wool and linen were coloured with dyes made from plants, fruits, insects and shellfish.
Aramaic was spoken across Palestine and Syria, but people from Galilee, Samaria and Judea each had their own accent and turns of phrase.
Rome kept troops in its provinces to keep order, and local people often resented their presence.
Wealthy Roman families owned many slaves, who worked as gardeners, cooks, maids, secretaries and tutors.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus spend the Sabbath at Nain?
o: Bargaining for robes in the village market all day
Sitting in the synagogue beside Justus
Riding ahead alone to look at Cana
Idle and bored while Justus went to the synagogue
quiz.e: Justus went to the synagogue alone and later talked with a woman and a young man he did not introduce; Marcellus felt snubbed.

quiz.q: Why did Justus hurry them along the road to Cana?
o: He had to reach Cana before the next Sabbath
He wanted Marcellus to hear a girl who sang at the fountain
He feared the Roman patrols that watched the highway after dark
He had promised to sell the homespun before sunset
quiz.e: Justus planned a surprise: Miriam, a crippled girl, sang every evening by the fountain in Cana.

quiz.q: According to Justus, when did Miriam’s great change come?
o: When a famous physician from Tiberias visited
After she bathed in the hot springs of the town
On the day of a friend’s wedding she refused to attend
When her parents took her to the Passover in Jerusalem
quiz.e: She wept all that day, but when her parents came home from the wedding-feast she met them with gladness, and sang.

quiz.q: Why, according to Justus, did the poor of Galilee have no use for hot springs?
o: They lacked the illnesses of rich food and wine
The priests forbade bathing in healing waters
The springs were owned by Herod’s family
They could not afford the long trip to Tiberias
quiz.e: Justus joked that only gluttons and winebibbers needed such cures, and the listening crowd laughed with him.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus react to Miriam’s singing at the fountain?
o: He thought her voice pleasant but untrained
He wept, deeply moved like those around him
He began sketching her face for a sculpture
He left early to avoid being noticed
quiz.e: Her deep contralto brought tears to his eyes, as it did to Justus and much of the crowd.

quiz.q: What did Miriam say sets anyone free?
o: The truth, which leaves the spirit free
Patience, which outlasts every hardship
Music, which lifts the heart above pain
Forgiveness, which ends every bitterness
quiz.e: Though her country had a foreign master and she could not walk, she said her spirit was free; her freedom was a gift, not something she earned.

quiz.q: What did Justus bring up while Naomi showed her weaving?
o: That Benjamin of Athens owed money to Benyosef
That Romans were forbidden by the priests to buy from Jewish weavers
That Miriam had been asking about Marcellus’ family
That a young Greek from Benyosef’s shop knew Benjamin too
quiz.e: Justus noticed Marcellus’ Samaritan turns of speech and mentioned Demetrius, the fugitive Greek who had learned Aramaic from Benjamin.

quiz.q: What did Miriam quietly ask Marcellus while her mother was away?
o: Whether he would carry a letter to Jerusalem
Whether he knew that Justus suspected him
Why he had lied to Justus about knowing the Greek
Whether he would buy all her mother’s robes
quiz.e: She saw he was no merchant and asked what he was really doing in Galilee; he answered, as she had earlier, “It is a secret.”

chapters.title: Toward Sepphoris
chapters.intro: Background on Jewish and Roman religion, the Temple in Jerusalem and the towns of Galilee, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A word or habit of speech belonging to one particular region.
Whether something is proper or fitting to do.
A sudden, intense but usually short-lived passion for someone.
Quietly longing for something, often with a touch of sadness.
A silver coin, and a unit of weight, used by the Jews and their neighbours.
The strap that goes under an animal’s belly to hold a saddle in place.
Someone who gives help or money to others.
Careful and sparing with money; plain and simple.
Treating serious things lightly or with careless humour.
A person who is smugly proud of their own goodness.
To fret or complain about something you have lost or cannot have.
Being completely full, especially after eating.
A tenth of one’s income or produce, given for religious purposes.
To disband an army and send its soldiers home.
The crime of betraying one’s ruler or country.
Jews worshipped a single, invisible God and regarded statues of other gods as idols, forbidden by the Commandments.
Romans honoured many gods with temples, altars and statues in streets and homes. Much Roman sculpture was copied from Greek models or made by Greek artists.
Jewish law forbids some foods, such as pork and shellfish, and sets rules for preparing others. Romans had no such rules.
A Hebrew title meaning “my master” or “my teacher”, given to teachers of the Jewish law.
An old and widespread belief that some people could bring harm or bad luck on others simply by looking at them.
In the outer courts of the Temple in Jerusalem, merchants sold animals for sacrifice and money-changers swapped pilgrims’ coins for the coinage accepted for Temple dues.
A town in Galilee, a few miles north of Nazareth.
A small hill village in Galilee, remembered in the Gospels as the home town of Jesus.
A fishing town on the north-western shore of the Lake of Galilee.
The everyday riding and pack animal of Palestine, cheap to keep and sure-footed on rough hill roads.
A labourer was usually hired by the day and paid at sunset; a denarius was a common day’s wage.
Short, simple stories that teach a moral or religious lesson; Jewish teachers often taught this way.
“Faithful are the wounds of a friend”
A saying from the Book of Proverbs: honest criticism from a friend is worth more than flattery from an enemy.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus do with the donkey Jasper on reaching Sepphoris?
o: Sold him to the village potter
Lent him to Justus for the journey
Gave him to Justus’ grandson Jonathan
Left him at Rebecca’s house to rest
quiz.e: He let Jonathan ride and then told him the donkey was his; Jonathan decided he must be “one of us” and said Jesus had straightened his foot.

quiz.q: Why was Jonathan troubled on the evening he got the donkey?
o: Jasper had bitten one of the village children
He had refused to let the lame boy Thomas ride
His mother had told him to give the donkey back
Rebecca had scolded him for missing supper
quiz.e: Thomas, on crutches, had asked to ride and Jonathan said no; Thomas was going home to Capernaum the next day, and Jonathan chose to give him Jasper.

quiz.q: Why was Justus unhappy when the neighbours praised Jonathan?
o: He thought Thomas’ mother should have refused the gift
He feared the Romans would hear of a crippled boy cured
He thought the donkey too valuable to be given away
He feared pride in his good deed would spoil the boy
quiz.e: Justus said no vanity damages a man’s character like pride over his good deeds, so they decided to take Jonathan away with them.

quiz.q: Why did Marcellus refuse Justus’ offer to take him to Nazareth?
o: He had heard the town was hostile to strangers
He wished to reach Capernaum before the Sabbath
Justus said there was no weaving to be had there
He had no wish to meet Jesus’ mother
quiz.e: Justus thought Jesus’ mother would talk freely with him, but Marcellus winced and said she would not want to speak of her son to a Roman.

quiz.q: According to Justus, how did Jesus come by his robe?
o: His mother wove it for him before he left Nazareth
Tamar wove it after he rebuilt the loom the authorities wrecked
A wealthy follower in Capernaum gave it to him
He bought it from a weaver at the Passover market
quiz.e: Tamar, an outcast suspected of witchcraft, had her loom destroyed for weaving on the Sabbath; Jesus rebuilt it and she wove him the Robe.

quiz.q: Where was Justus when Jesus died?
o: In prison, accused of picking up Temple coins
At home in Sepphoris, caring for his grandson
Hiding in Bethany with the other disciples
On the road back from the Passover in Jerusalem
quiz.e: After Jesus drove the traders out of the Temple, some of his friends were jailed on a false charge of gathering the scattered coins; it was all over when they were freed.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus respond to Justus’ story of the wedding at Cana?
o: He refused to believe the water had become wine
He asked to meet the servants who had poured it
He said he had heard the same tale in Jerusalem
He took it as proof that Jesus was a magician
quiz.e: Marcellus protested that the tale “spoils the story of Jesus”, suggesting that water merely tasted like wine in his presence.

quiz.q: What connection did Marcellus make on the hilltop on the way to Cana?
o: That Hariph the potter was Miriam’s uncle
That Justus had been at the wedding himself
That Jesus came late to the wedding on the day Miriam first sang
That the Roman soldiers had come looking for Jesus at the wedding at Cana
quiz.e: Miriam found her voice on the day of Anna’s wedding, when Jesus arrived late; Justus thought it possible she had been asked to keep it secret.

chapters.title: Back in Cana
chapters.intro: Background on Roman rule in Judea and Galilee, tax collectors, Jericho and Jewish wedding feasts, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A meeting place, or an arranged meeting.
Countrified; to do with rustic, rural life.
A disease of the hock, the middle joint of an animal’s hind leg, that can make it lame.
An old word for paralysis, often with trembling.
A soldier who acts as an officer’s personal servant.
Unable to make up one’s mind; wavering.
An old word for a rabbit. In old English Bibles it names the rock hyrax, a small rock-dwelling animal.
Giving back what was taken, or paying for a loss or injury.
Someone with leprosy, an ancient name for several serious skin diseases. Lepers were shunned and had to live apart.
To take back publicly something you have said or believed.
The Roman governor of Judea, who lived at Caesarea on the coast and came up to Jerusalem at the great festivals to keep order.
A son of Herod the Great who ruled Galilee as tetrarch under Rome.
The head of the Temple priesthood in Jerusalem and of the Jewish council. Under Roman rule high priests were appointed and removed by the Romans.
Local men who collected tolls and taxes for Rome or its client rulers. They were despised as collaborators and often as cheats.
A Roman officer commanding a century, a unit of about eighty to a hundred soldiers.
An ancient oasis town in the Jordan valley, north of the Dead Sea, known for its palms and gardens.
A fishing town near where the River Jordan flows into the north end of the Lake of Galilee.
A town on the north-western shore of the Lake of Galilee.
A large Greek island in the eastern Mediterranean, then part of a Roman province.
Caravans carried goods across the deserts of the Near East on camels, and the animals themselves were bought and sold at markets.
Potters made large earthenware jars that might hold water, wine or oil.
A Jewish wedding was celebrated with a feast for family and neighbours, sometimes lasting several days. Running short of food or wine was a great embarrassment for the host.
Rich Romans cooled their wine with snow brought down from the mountains, an extravagant luxury.

quiz.q: Why was Jesse, the son of Beoni, going to Jerusalem?
o: To sell homespun in the bazaars at Passover
To visit his brother in the prison there
To buy camels at the auction after Passover
To visit kinsmen who lived near the Temple
quiz.e: He went every year to the camel auction, where caravans sold off their pack-animals cheaply, and agreed to carry Marcellus’ letter.

quiz.q: What did the centurion Hortensius do when Jesse admitted his camel was spavined?
o: He offered to split the cost of the flaw
He refused to buy any of the camels
He reported Jesse to the fort’s commander
He demanded the camel at half price
quiz.e: Struck by Jesse’s honesty, Hortensius guessed he knew Jesus and paid seventy shekels instead of sixty.

quiz.q: What news about Pilate did Justus pass on to Jesse?
o: He had been made governor of all Syria
He had been recalled to Rome in disgrace
He had become a secret follower of Jesus
He had been sent away sick, perhaps in mind
quiz.e: Rumour said Pilate had not appeared in public since the crucifixion and had been sent to Crete; Benyosef thought his sickness was mental.

quiz.q: Why was Justus so dismayed at the rumour about the Commander at Minoa?
o: He had once been imprisoned at Minoa by that very officer
The legion from Minoa had put Jesus to death
Minoa’s troops were known for plundering villages
The man had once arrested Benyosef’s friends
quiz.e: Hearing that Paulus might take over at Capernaum, Justus muttered “They wouldn’t dare!”, which convinced Marcellus he could never confess his part to Miriam.

quiz.q: How had Miriam worked out that Marcellus was interested in Jesus?
o: Justus had told her in confidence at the vineyard
He chose Justus as guide and knew the Greek from Benyosef’s
Demetrius had written to her from Jerusalem
She had seen the Robe among his belongings
quiz.e: She noted he knew nothing of textiles or bargaining, had picked Justus, and was linked to the Greek at Benyosef’s shop, where Jesus’ friends met.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus tell Miriam had most impressed him about Jesus?
o: His kindness to the poor and the lame of Galilee
His wisdom in answering the priests at the trial
His power to heal those whom the doctors had failed
His fearless courage when everyone was against him
quiz.e: He spoke of Jesus’ effortless courage: utterly fearless, with a lost cause and certain death before him.

quiz.q: Why did Miriam say she did not regret her lameness?
o: Her songs from her cot helped people more than if she were well
She believed it was a punishment she must bear patiently for her sins
It kept her from marrying a man she did not love
Her parents had grown kinder since her illness
quiz.e: If she were whole, people might say singing was easy for her; from her cot she lifts them in their own troubles, and she lives among love.

quiz.q: In Miriam’s story, what did Zacchaeus do after Jesus dined with him?
o: He had Jesus arrested by the Roman guard at the gate
He paid for a feast for the whole waiting crowd
He gave half his goods to the poor and made amends
He left Jericho and was never seen there again
quiz.e: The hated chief tax-collector of Jericho came out humbled, promising half his goods to the poor and restitution to those he had defrauded.

quiz.q: What did Miriam urge Justus to do once Marcellus had left the arbor?
o: Send Marcellus away before he could hurt her
Take Marcellus to Nazareth to meet Jesus’ mother
Ask Reuben to forbid the Roman from coming back
Tell Marcellus everything, including the work now going on
quiz.e: She felt he had a right to know the rest of the story and the work being done in Jerusalem, Joppa and Caesarea; Justus promised to tell him.

quiz.q: Why did Marcellus say he believed Hariph’s story of the five thousand?
o: He trusted Hariph more than he trusted Justus
Jesus had moved selfish people to share their food
Hariph showed him the baskets of fragments
The disciples had secretly brought bread from Capernaum
quiz.e: Hearing how Hariph shared his bread after a boy offered his basket, Marcellus declared the miracle was making one family out of a stingy crowd.

chapters.title: The Road to Capernaum
chapters.intro: Background on Galilee and its lake, Jewish customs, early belief and the Roman army, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

Dragged or pulled along, often by force.
Sluggishness; a lack of energy or interest.

Of the countryside and farm life, sometimes with a hint of being simple or rustic.
The lengthwise threads stretched on a loom, through which the crosswise threads are woven.
In the Roman provinces, a tax collector; such men were widely disliked.
The side of something, such as a rock or hill, that is sheltered from the wind.
Truthfulness; whether something really happened as told.
A narrow band of cloth worn around the head.
A metal cuff for the wrist, chained to hold a prisoner.

A fishing town on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee. The Gospels place much of Jesus’ teaching and healing there.
A city on the western shore of the lake, built by Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee, and named in honour of the Emperor Tiberius.
An ancient port on the Mediterranean coast of Palestine, today part of Tel Aviv–Jaffa.

A Roman soldier could compel a civilian to carry his baggage for a set distance. The custom was much resented in the provinces.

Slaves were sometimes marked as property, for example by branding, especially after trying to run away. Under the law of Moses, a servant who chose to stay with his master for life had his ear pierced with an awl.
A ritual washing in water, as a sign of being made clean and starting anew. John the Baptist practised it in the river Jordan.
Greek for “the anointed one”, a translation of the Hebrew “Messiah”. In ancient Israel kings and priests were anointed with oil when they took office.
A student or follower who learns from a teacher by living and travelling with him.
The main unit of the Roman army, about 5,000 heavy infantry, each legion with its own number and name.
An officer who commanded a century, a unit of about 80 men.
A senior commander, usually in charge of a legion or a province’s troops.
The commander’s headquarters in a Roman camp or fort.

quiz.q: How did Jesus first greet old Bartholomew in his fig orchard?
o: He called him Nathanael, a name no one had used in years
He asked him for a drink of water from his garden well
He called him “Rabbi” and asked to sit at his feet
He told him that his long years of waiting were over
quiz.e: Jesus cheerily called him Nathanael, which no one had done for some forty years, and the astonished old man became a disciple.

quiz.q: According to Justus, how was the widow Lydia healed?
o: Jesus came to her house after visiting Jairus’ daughter
She bathed in a healing spring her family took her to
Simon laid his hands on her as the crowd passed by
She reached through the crowd and touched Jesus’ Robe
quiz.e: Lydia forced her way through the crowd and touched his Robe; Jesus asked “Who touched me?” and told her, “Your faith has made you whole.”

quiz.q: How did Marcellus answer when Justus finished Lydia’s story?
o: He said her illness had probably run its course that day
He said, in all sincerity, that he believed every word
He said it was beautiful but could not possibly be true
He asked whether he might meet Lydia in Capernaum
quiz.e: Justus expected a common-sense explanation, but Marcellus said, “I believe every word of it!” He only tried to explain it away later that night.

quiz.q: Who was the shabby, bearded man Marcellus saw near the camp before dawn?
o: Demetrius, disguised in patched clothes and a sailor’s cap
A Capernaum fisherman whom Justus had arranged to meet
A legionary from the fort sent to watch the travellers
Simon the tanner, carrying a message from Joppa
quiz.e: It was Demetrius, who had learned in Cana where Marcellus was going and wanted to see him alone before meeting Justus.

quiz.q: What did Demetrius confess he had done soon after he was baptized?
o: He stole bread from a market stall on the road to Joppa
He lied to Stephanos about where he planned to hide afterward
He broke a legionary’s lance instead of carrying his pack
He struck a Temple guard who insulted the disciples
quiz.e: A soldier ordered him to carry his pack and thrust at him with a lance when he refused; Demetrius took the lance and broke it, “before my hair was dry.”

quiz.q: Why did Justus leave the breakfast table to stand beside Demetrius?
o: He wanted to ask Demetrius privately about Jerusalem
He was angered by Marcellus treating slavery so casually
Jonathan had been rude to the stranger and he felt ashamed
He suspected Demetrius was a spy sent from the fort
quiz.e: When Marcellus told Jonathan that Demetrius “likes to stand up when he eats,” Justus, who hated slavery, said it was not funny and went to stand with the slave.

quiz.q: Why did the legionary in Tiberias arrest Demetrius?
o: Demetrius had insulted him in front of the food-stall cook
A notice at the fort named Demetrius as a runaway slave wanted for assault
He recognised Demetrius from the brawling troops from Minoa
The cook called him a thief, and a prisoner would excuse his night away
quiz.e: The cook claimed the shabby slave with money must be a thief, and the hung-over soldier hoped a prisoner would cover for his night away from the fort.

quiz.q: What news did the legionary in the opposite cell give Demetrius?
o: Old Julian had ordered all Greek slaves in Galilee to be held
The fort’s prisoners were to be marched to Jerusalem for trial
Tribune Paulus from Minoa was now the fort’s new Legate
A slave had broken out of the fort the night before and was hunted
quiz.e: Julian had been transferred to Jerusalem; the new Legate was Paulus, whose men from Minoa had brawled with the garrison and filled the guardhouse.

chapters.title: Bartholomew’s Fig Orchard
chapters.intro: Background on Jewish life, Galilee and its lake, and Roman rule in the provinces, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: This chapter includes a knife fight in a prison and a flogging being ordered.
Using more words than are needed; long-windedness.
A violent storm with strong winds.
The bar or handle used to turn a boat’s rudder and steer it.
A small triangular sail set at the front of a boat.
Scooping water out of a boat with a bucket or bowl to keep it afloat.
A beach of small, smooth pebbles.
A dizzy feeling that the room is spinning.
A raised platform at one end of a hall, for a seat of honour or a judge.
Too eager to please or obey; fawning.
An inn or lodging house for travellers.
A tomb, especially one cut into rock.
An official order issued by someone in authority.
A local meeting house where Jews gathered for prayer and the reading and teaching of scripture.
A Jewish movement devoted to careful keeping of the Law of Moses, including traditions handed down by word of mouth. They were influential among ordinary people.
Priests, descended from Aaron, offered the sacrifices at the Temple in Jerusalem. Levites, from the tribe of Levi, assisted them as singers, gatekeepers and servants.
People of Samaria, between Judea and Galilee. They shared the books of Moses with the Jews but worshipped on their own holy mountain, and the two peoples had long been hostile.
A tenth of one’s harvest or income, given for the support of religion. The Law of Moses required tithes.
Boats on the Sea of Galilee were wooden, worked by oars and a sail, and crewed by several men. Fishermen often worked their nets at night.
A fishing village near the northern end of the Sea of Galilee, close to where the Jordan flows into the lake.
In the Hebrew Bible, every man sitting “under his vine and under his fig tree” is a picture of peace and security.
The road from Jerusalem down to Jericho drops steeply through lonely desert hills and was notorious for robbers.
Literally “ruler of a quarter”: a ruler of part of a divided kingdom, under Rome’s authority.
A son of Herod the Great who ruled Galilee and Peraea as tetrarch, with Rome’s approval. He built the city of Tiberias.
Roman officers stationed in a province sometimes gave money for local buildings. The Gospels mention a centurion who built a synagogue at Capernaum.
A senior Roman commander, usually in charge of a legion or a province’s troops.

quiz.q: Why couldn’t Marcellus simply dismiss Bartholomew’s story of the storm?
o: He had seen a storm end just as suddenly on his voyage
The old man was neither a liar nor a fool, and was in the boat
Justus had already shown him a written account of it
Several fishermen in Capernaum told the very same tale
quiz.e: Bartholomew was an eyewitness, neither lying nor deluded, and he was not trying to persuade anyone; that made the story impossible to wave away.

quiz.q: What did Bartholomew admit he shouted to Jesus as the boat filled with water?
o: That he should take the tiller and steer for Bethsaida
That they must throw the heavy nets overboard at once
That Simon wanted to beach the boat in the nearest cove
That they were sinking, and did Jesus not even care?
quiz.e: He cried, “We are going to drown! … Don’t you care?” and still winced at having said it to his Master.

quiz.q: What started the fight in Demetrius’ prison cell?
o: A Syrian slave tried to take the money Marcellus gave him
Demetrius tried to push past the guards when the door opened
A Syrian poured his water away instead of letting him drink
The old guard struck him for talking to the next cell
quiz.e: Desperate with thirst, Demetrius held out his bowl; the Syrian spilled the water over him and his feet, and Demetrius struck him with the bowl.

quiz.q: What did Paulus want to know about Marcellus when he questioned Demetrius?
o: Whether he was well in his head, after a rumour
Whether he still owed Sextus money from their dice games
Whether he had come to Galilee on the Emperor’s orders
Whether he had sold the Robe he won at the crucifixion
quiz.e: Paulus asked whether Marcellus was “well—in his head”, remembering that something “cracked” when he put on the Robe at the Procurator’s banquet.

quiz.q: At supper, why did Justus say he was always looking about him, at every door and hill-crest?
o: He feared that spies from the Temple were following him
He was watching for Demetrius, who should have joined them
He had promised Lydia he would watch for her nephew
He believed Jesus was alive and expected to meet him
quiz.e: Justus whispered that Jesus had come alive on the third day, and said he was always looking for him, at every door and turn of the road.

quiz.q: What did Justus say Thomas declared just before Jesus appeared at Benyosef’s house?
o: That they should all leave Jerusalem before they were arrested
That he would not believe until he saw and touched the wounds
That John’s account was the truest he had heard so far
That he had seen Jesus himself on the road to the city
quiz.e: Thomas shouted that he would not believe without seeing Jesus and touching his wounds; then Jesus stood at his elbow and held out his hands.

quiz.q: After Shalum told the parable of the Samaritan, what question did Marcellus raise?
o: Why a priest and a Levite would walk past a man left half-dead
Whether Samaritans were truly as hated as Shalum said
What the Samaritan should do if he arrived during the attack
Whether the innkeeper was ever repaid for his trouble
quiz.e: Knowing Jesus forbade fighting, he asked whether the Samaritan should defend the victim or wait until the robbers had finished; Justus said Jesus cared for binding wounds, not inflicting them.

quiz.q: Why was Justus so distressed when the legionary brought a message to the tent?
o: He learned Marcellus was a Roman Tribune and felt he had betrayed his friends
He thought the soldier had come to arrest him for speaking of Jesus
The message said that Demetrius had been badly hurt at the fort
He realised the Pharisees at the inn had overheard their whole talk
quiz.e: The message called Marcellus “Tribune”, and Justus moaned that he had delivered his friends to their enemies; at dawn he took Jonathan home.

chapters.title: The Fort at Capernaum
chapters.intro: Background on Roman life and letters, the Herod family and the cities of Palestine, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: Noisy, rowdy merrymaking, usually with drinking.
A person who flatters powerful people to win favour.
Saying very little; silent by habit.
Too great or wonderful to be put into words.
Words chanted as a magic spell.
Harmless; not likely to cause trouble.
Rude or disrespectful, especially to someone of higher standing.
Latin for “time flies”. The phrase comes from a line in Virgil’s poem on farming, the Georgics, and was often carved on sundials.
Rome’s most celebrated poet, who wrote the Aeneid, the epic of Rome’s legendary founding, in the time of Augustus.
The formal outer garment of a Roman citizen: a large piece of white wool wrapped around the body and over one shoulder.
Romans loved gambling with dice, shaken in a cup and thrown on a table, even though betting was officially frowned upon.
King of Judea under Roman protection, famous for grand building projects including the rebuilding of the Temple in Jerusalem. After his death his kingdom was divided among his sons.
A son of Herod the Great who ruled Galilee and Peraea as tetrarch. He built Tiberias on the Sea of Galilee as his capital.
The wife of Herod Antipas. She had earlier been married to his half-brother, and the marriage scandalised many Jews.
The high council of Jewish elders, priests and scholars in Jerusalem, which judged religious matters.
An ancient city near the Mediterranean coast in the far south of Palestine, on the road to Egypt, with a busy harbour.
A region east of the river Jordan, ruled together with Galilee by Herod Antipas.
An oasis city in the Jordan valley, north of the Dead Sea, famous for its palms and balsam.
The capital of the Roman province of Syria and one of the largest cities of the Empire, home to many Jews and Greeks.

quiz.q: Why had Paulus been so glad of his appointment to Capernaum?
o: He hoped to win quick promotion by crushing the Christians
Herod Antipas had asked for him by name for the post
It brought a large rise in pay and a palace of his own
Minoa was a disgrace, and Capernaum was said to be lovely
quiz.e: Minoa was a dusty, degrading posting; Capernaum was said to be beautiful, near Herod’s court at Tiberias, with docile people.

quiz.q: What soon made Paulus restless in his new command?
o: Constant brawling between his men and the townspeople
The deep quiet of the place and the lack of any diversion
Quarrels with Herod’s deputy over the supply of wine
The heat and the fevers that rose from the lake every summer
quiz.e: Once the Minoa contingent had gone, the fort fell oppressively silent; the town slept, the Herod family was away, and time seemed to stand still.

quiz.q: How did Paulus react when Demetrius admitted beating Tribune Quintus?
o: He was delighted and wanted every detail, since he despised Quintus
He ordered him held in chains and shipped to Rome to stand trial there
He said Marcellus must pay heavy damages to Quintus’ family
He refused to believe a slave could have done such a thing
quiz.e: Paulus, who loathed Quintus as a strutting peacock, leaned forward beaming and drew out the whole story, though he warned it was a capital crime.

quiz.q: What did Demetrius tell Paulus he believed about Jesus?
o: That he was a great teacher, but no more than a man
That his followers had hidden his body after he died
That he had died, was now alive, and was a god
That he would soon return to drive Rome from the land
quiz.e: Demetrius said he was sure Jesus died and sure he was alive, and that he was, and is, a god; Paulus called him crazy but released him.

quiz.q: What did Paulus apologise to Marcellus for over their wine?
o: Putting him in an unhappy position at the Procurator’s banquet
Keeping Demetrius locked up for a night in the fort
Failing to write to him while he was so long ill
Sending a soldier to fetch him so late in the evening
quiz.e: Paulus still reproached himself for the drunken night when Marcellus put on the Robe, and said he was sorry it happened.

quiz.q: What point did Marcellus make by comparing the stories of Jesus with the deeds of kings?
o: That kings had always claimed magic powers to scare people
That Jesus wanted a throne as much as any other ruler
That Tiberius would surely want to meet such a man himself
That Jesus only healed and restored, while kings maimed and blinded
quiz.e: He noted Jesus made the blind see and never made anyone blind; Paulus agreed kings were destroyers and half-wished the tale were true.

quiz.q: Why did Marcellus beg Paulus not to tell Herod about Miriam?
o: Miriam’s family had already been threatened by Herod’s men
He wanted to bring Miriam to Rome to sing for the Emperor
She was gently bred and would be degraded at Herod’s court
Herod would arrest her as a follower of Jesus at once
quiz.e: Paulus thought she might sing at one of Herod’s banquets; Marcellus hotly refused to let his friend be exposed to that household.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus answer Paulus’ advice to leave quietly for Joppa?
o: He agreed to sail home in the morning with an escort
He said he would go to Jerusalem to talk with the leaders
He said he would stay on in Galilee to finish buying homespun
He asked Paulus for a letter to protect Demetrius
quiz.e: Marcellus refused to leave Palestine until he had satisfied himself about the resurrection, and announced he was going to Jerusalem.

chapters.title: Through the Damascus Gate
chapters.intro: Background on Jerusalem, Jewish and early Christian life, and Rome’s generals and games, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: This chapter includes violence by soldiers and by a mob, with deaths.
Speed and efficiency in getting something done.
To speak of something as having little worth.
In a playful, knowing, slightly teasing way.
The habit of saying very little.
Excessive eagerness to serve or please others.
Very harsh criticism; a severe scolding.
Money or food given to the poor as charity.
The great gate in Jerusalem’s northern wall, named for the road that leads from it north towards Damascus.
The great Temple of Jerusalem, rebuilt on a grand scale by Herod the Great: the centre of Jewish worship, with broad courts and steps where crowds and beggars gathered.
An Aramaic name meaning “place of a skull”: the place of execution outside Jerusalem’s walls where, according to the Gospels, Jesus was crucified.
Greek for “assembly”, originally a meeting of citizens. It later became the usual word for “church”.
Greek for “brother”. The first Christians called one another brothers and sisters.
The Book of Acts describes the first believers in Jerusalem selling property and sharing everything so that no one among them was in need.
Speaking against God or treating what is holy with contempt; under Jewish law a grave offence.
A Hebrew prophet. The book bearing his name contains famous poems about a light shining on people in darkness and a child born to rule, which Christians read as pointing to Jesus.
A popular Roman general, adopted son of the Emperor Tiberius, celebrated for his campaigns against the Germans.
Rome’s huge stadium for chariot races, where vast crowds roared at the spectacle.
Citizenship brought legal privileges, such as protection from some punishments. It could be inherited, so citizens were born in cities far from Rome.

quiz.q: How did Demetrius answer, on the journey south, when Marcellus called the resurrection impossible?
o: He agreed it could not happen, yet said it had happened
He said Marcellus would understand once he saw Jesus too
He quoted the prophets to prove that it had been foretold
He refused to discuss it again for the rest of the journey
quiz.e: Demetrius cheerfully conceded every objection: “The thing couldn’t happen; but it did.” Marcellus realised he was really arguing with himself.

quiz.q: To what did Demetrius compare faith at the end of their talk on the road?
o: A deed to a house, held for ever with full rights of ownership
A sail that carries a ship safely home through any storm
A kit of tools, worth only what a man builds with them
A coin that buys entry to a kingdom somewhere else
quiz.e: He said faith is not like a deed to a house but like a kit of tools: worth what a man does with them, and worthless when laid down.

quiz.q: What is the Ecclesia, as Rhoda describes it to Demetrius?
o: Benyosef’s shop, where the disciples meet late each night
A school in the Temple courts where Simon teaches the young
A house outside the city where believers hide from soldiers
An old bazaar where Christians gather to share supper every evening
quiz.e: The Christians leased Nathan’s old bazaar; hundreds came to the shared supper, and Stephanos named it the Ecclesia because so many were Greeks.

quiz.q: What did Stephanos believe had gone wrong with the Ecclesia?
o: The priests had sent in spies who stirred up the Greeks against the Jews
Letting anyone sell up and live there drew idle, quarrelsome people
Simon had kept too much of the money for himself
The other disciples refused to help Simon run it
quiz.e: Simon’s plan that believers sell their property and live together had turned it into a free boarding-house full of bickering Jews and Greeks.

quiz.q: What did Stephanos boldly declare to Marcellus while holding the Robe?
o: That Jesus had forgiven him, and he could make amends
That he must hand the Robe over to the disciples at once
That the Robe had healed Stephanos of an illness
That Marcellus would one day be put to death for it
quiz.e: Stephanos said, “You killed my Lord,” but that it was forgivable, that he had heard Jesus forgive him, and urged him to make friends with Jesus.

quiz.q: Why did Marcellus call the innkeeper Levi “a mean fellow”?
o: He had told the soldiers which of his guests were Christians
He charged Marcellus double for a room during the search
He made the dead old man’s daughter serve breakfast
He boasted that he would be paid for every arrest
quiz.e: The slave-girl serving his table was the daughter of the old man killed in the courtyard, and Levi said it was simply her regular task.

quiz.q: What did Simon call out as the legionaries took him from the Ecclesia?
o: That they should all leave Jerusalem before nightfall
That Stephanos would lead them while he was gone
That they must fight back rather than let the soldiers take him
To be of good cheer, make no resistance, and he would return
quiz.e: Simon told his people to take heart and not resist, promising to come back; the Centurion retorted that they would not see him again.

quiz.q: What did Stephanos cry out just before he died?
o: That he saw Jesus, and asked his Lord to take him
That his killers should be forgiven, for they knew no better
That Marcellus must carry the Robe back to Rome
That the Temple would be destroyed for this
quiz.e: Raising himself up, he shouted, “I see him! … My Lord Jesus—take me!” and Marcellus became convinced he truly saw Jesus.

quiz.q: How did Simon at first understand his escape from prison?
o: He believed a guard he had once healed had freed him
He thought it was a vivid dream until he stumbled in the street
He thought the soldiers meant to kill him outside the walls
He assumed Marcellus had paid the guards to let him go
quiz.e: Chains fell off and doors opened silently, so he was sure he was dreaming; only after the jolt of stumbling on a curb did he know he was free.

quiz.q: What happened on the Temple steps as Peter and Marcellus walked back from Golgotha?
o: Temple guards recognised Peter and tried to seize him
A beggar told them where the soldiers had taken Stephanos
Peter made a man crippled from birth stand up and walk
Peter preached to the crowd about the death of Stephanos
quiz.e: Having no money, Peter told the beggar, “In the name of Jesus—stand up—and walk!” and the man walked, astonishing Marcellus.

chapters.title: Rome by Night
chapters.intro: Background on the city of Rome, the Roman household, and myth and divination at the Emperor’s court, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

items: A harsh, jarring mixture of loud sounds.
Cheap and showy, made only to tempt buyers.
A scene of noisy uproar and confusion.
Abnormally thin and weak, from illness or hunger.
Openly showing one’s feelings, especially affection.
Someone who spreads ideas to win people over to a cause.
A ruler giving up the throne or the duties of power.
A hot, moist cloth or poultice laid on the body to ease pain.
Very pale and thin, like a corpse.
Made of small square tiles fitted together, as in a mosaic.
Concerned with abstract questions about reality, the soul or the supernatural.
Rome’s port at the mouth of the river Tiber, where sea-going ships unloaded goods and passengers for the city.
A law dating from Julius Caesar’s time banned most wheeled carts from Rome’s streets by day, so heavy wagons rumbled through the city at night.
The first Roman emperor, remembered for lavish building and spectacles. Tiberius, his stepson and adopted heir, succeeded him.
The Floralia, a lively spring festival in honour of Flora, goddess of flowers, with games and theatre shows.
A rocky island in the Bay of Naples (Neapolis) where the Emperor Tiberius lived in seclusion in his later years.
The large central hall of a Roman house, where visitors were received.
An open garden courtyard surrounded by a row of columns, at the heart of a wealthy house.
A long, flowing dress worn by Roman women of standing over their under-tunic.
A great Roman house kept dozens of slaves, each with a set task: steward, butler, grooms, maids, gardeners, door-keepers.
Roman diviners called haruspices examined the entrails, especially the liver, of sacrificed animals to learn the will of the gods.
In Greek myth, the river of the underworld that the souls of the dead must cross.
In Greek myth, the fleece of a magical golden ram, sought by the hero Jason and his Argonauts.
In Greek legend, the hollow wooden horse in which Greek soldiers hid to enter and capture the city of Troy.
In the Hebrew Bible, the garden where God placed the first man and woman.

quiz.q: What did the rude crowds on the way home from the dock make Marcellus think about?
o: How much he had missed the life and bustle of the capital
His claim that good will would begin with the common people
Whether Demetrius would be safe in Rome after the Quintus affair
How the Emperor might punish him for staying so long away
quiz.e: He had told Paulus the new kingdom would begin with the common people; here they were, a selfish shoving mob, and the thought mocked him.

quiz.q: What did Lucia and Demetrius disagree about in the atrium?
o: Whether Marcellus was truly well again after his illness
Who should serve the late supper in the banquet-room
Whether Demetrius ought to be punished for the Quintus affair
Whether the servants should be allowed to be so merry
quiz.e: Lucia feared the slaves would be spoiled by their happiness; Demetrius said it might not hurt them to be really happy for once.

quiz.q: What did Marcipor reveal to Demetrius in the moonlit peristyle?
o: There were already Christians in Rome, and he was one of them
The Senator had arranged for Diana to marry Prince Gaius instead
Decimus had been spying on Marcellus’ letters from abroad
The Emperor had ordered Demetrius to be arrested on arrival
quiz.e: The story had reached Rome months before through merchants from Antioch, and Marcipor had come to believe.

quiz.q: Why did Marcipor want the Roman Christians kept secret from Marcellus?
o: He feared Marcellus would report their meetings to the patrols
The Christians in Rome did not trust any Roman officer
He feared Marcellus would join them and break with his father
He wanted Demetrius to tell Marcellus himself later
quiz.e: Decimus had already described the movement to the Senator as a revolt, and Marcipor did not want Marcellus to offend his ageing father.

quiz.q: What did Senator Gallio advise Marcellus to tell the Emperor?
o: Nothing at all about Jesus, but only about the homespun
Jesus’ wise sayings and magic tales, but not his return to life
That he had been deceived by the Galileans and was sorry
Everything, since Tiberius would surely reward the truth
quiz.e: Gallio said Tiberius would enjoy the wonders, but believing in a resurrection would make Marcellus “one more monkey” in his menagerie.

quiz.q: How did the Senator respond when Marcellus declared that he too was a Christian?
o: He shouted that Marcellus was no longer his son
He forbade him to go to Capri to see the Emperor
He laughed and said the sea air would cure him
He turned and left the room without a word
quiz.e: Gallio made no reply; he turned away slowly and left without a backward glance, and Marcellus grieved over his father’s disappointment.

quiz.q: Why did the Empress Julia want Diana to marry Gaius?
o: Gallus’ hold on the army and Tiberius’ fondness for Diana would secure Gaius
Diana’s family was rich enough to pay off Gaius’ many debts
Celia had begged her to take Gaius away from Diana for good
Tiberius had promised Diana a villa if she married into the family
quiz.e: Julia told Celia that Gallus was the army, and that the Emperor’s love for Diana would practically ensure her son’s succession.

quiz.q: What did Diana beg Marcellus to do in the pergola?
o: Persuade the Emperor to send her home to her mother
Take her away from Capri, even if they had to bribe a boat
Keep away from Gaius, who had threatened to have him killed
Tell Tiberius that Dodinius was a fraud and a liar
quiz.e: Feeling unsafe and nearly mad on the island, she asked him to slip away with her; he refused to make them fugitives and asked her to be patient.

quiz.q: What choice did Tiberius put to Marcellus?
o: Join his council of sages or return to the army abroad
Sell Demetrius to him or see the slave put to death
Prove Jesus was alive or be banished from Rome
Give up his talk of Jesus or give up Diana
quiz.e: The Emperor would not let Diana marry a “fool”: Marcellus must abandon the Jesus talk or lose her, and decide by noon the next day.

quiz.q: What did Tiberius do when Marcellus offered him the Robe?
o: He put it on at once to prove he was not afraid of it
He ordered it burned as a dangerous piece of sorcery
He drew back his hand and told them to take it away
He gave it to Dodinius to examine for omens
quiz.e: After daring talk, the old man reached out, then recoiled, hid his hand under the covers and muttered, “Take it away!”

chapters.title: Breakfast with the Emperor
chapters.intro: Background on the island of Capri, Rome’s provinces and early Christian belief, plus vocabulary. Nothing here describes what happens in the chapter.

To talk aloud to oneself, as if no one else were there.
A tendency to lose one’s temper easily.
Bold daring, often of a rude or shocking kind.
Treating a serious matter too lightly, as if it were a joke.
Greedy and grasping; taking by force.
To rob a place violently, especially in war.
To criticise someone in an insulting, abusive way.
In an over-eager, fawning way, trying too hard to please.
Respectfully, giving way to someone of higher rank.
A rocky island at the southern edge of the Bay of Naples. The emperor Tiberius withdrew there in his old age and governed the empire from his villas on the island.
The “Villa of Jupiter”, the largest of the imperial villas on Capri, built high on the island’s north-eastern cliffs.
Rulers often spoke of themselves as “we” rather than “I”, a habit that stresses their office rather than their person.
A military tribune was a senior officer in a Roman legion. Young men of wealthy families often held the post early in a public career.
Greek for “the Anointed One”, a translation of the Hebrew word Messiah.
In Jewish hope, a king or deliverer anointed by God, often expected to free Israel and bring justice.
The name given to those who followed Jesus as the Christ. The Book of Acts says it was first used at Antioch.
Taxes and payments that conquered peoples and provinces had to send to Rome.
The Roman name for lands roughly covering modern France and Belgium.
A Roman province in south-western Gaul.
The Roman name for the Iberian peninsula, modern Spain and Portugal.
A region north of the Aegean Sea, covering parts of modern Bulgaria, Greece and Turkey.
Regions of Asia Minor (modern Turkey): Cappadocia in the central uplands, Pontus along the southern shore of the Black Sea.
Publius Vergilius Maro, the great Roman poet of the age of Augustus.
Virgil’s epic poem about the Trojan hero Aeneas, legendary ancestor of the Romans. It opens with the words “I sing of arms and the man.”

quiz.q: Why did the Emperor’s summons to breakfast distress Diana?
o: She feared he would order her back to Rome at once
She had quarrelled bitterly with him the night before
It meant missing her morning meeting with Marcellus
She knew the Empress would be at the table with them
quiz.e: She had been counting the hours until her early meeting with Marcellus in the pergola, and now it had to be put off.

quiz.q: According to Tiberius, what did Marcellus now believe about Jesus?
o: That he is divine and will rule the world without armies
That he was a wise teacher whose ideas died with him
That he survived the cross and then fled in secret to Egypt
That he will raise an army to drive Rome from Judea
quiz.e: Tiberius told Diana that Marcellus thought Jesus a god who would take command of the world without armies.

quiz.q: What choice had Tiberius put to Marcellus the night before?
o: Serve on Capri for life, or go back to the fort at Minoa
Give up Diana, or be stripped of his rank as a Tribune
Join the Emperor’s guard, or face a charge of treason
Abandon the Christians, or see Diana given to Gaius
quiz.e: Tiberius said that unless Marcellus gave up the Christian party at once, he would give Diana in marriage to Gaius.

quiz.q: Setting aside his prepared speech, which story did Marcellus tell Diana first?
o: How Lydia was healed by touching the Robe
How Jonathan gave up his donkey to Thomas
How Stephanos saw Jesus after his death
How Miriam found her voice at a wedding
quiz.e: He began simply, with Jonathan and the donkey; Diana thought it a mean thing to do to a little boy.

quiz.q: What explanation did Diana offer for the Robe healing Marcellus’ mind?
o: He had simply been ready to get well by then
He knew it had belonged to another lonely man
Some drug must have been left in the cloth
Demetrius had quietly nursed him back to health
quiz.e: Diana suggested it was because he knew it had belonged to another lonely man, which matched what Marcellus had felt.

quiz.q: After hearing the whole story, what did Diana ask of Marcellus?
o: To take her to Galilee to meet the people he described
To keep every word of it secret from the Emperor
To write it all down so that she could read it alone
To let it stay a mystery and live as if it hadn’t happened
quiz.e: She called it a beautiful mystery and asked that they live for each other as if it hadn’t happened; Marcellus said he could not.

quiz.q: How did Tiberius react when Marcellus came to him at noon?
o: He dismissed him, shouting that he was a brave fool
He offered him a post in Rome if he kept quiet
He had him arrested and charged with treason
He begged him to think again for Diana’s sake
quiz.e: Seeing his decision in his face, Tiberius sent him away, screaming that he was a fool who would die for his folly, a “brave, brave fool”.

quiz.q: Why could Marcellus not see Demetrius before he left Capri?
o: He had already sailed ahead with all the luggage
He had been sent across the island to guard Diana
He had been locked up after fighting the Nubians
He had gone into hiding when the guards arrived
quiz.e: The Chamberlain said the Greek had fought so hard against the packing of his master’s things that he had to be confined.

chapters.title: The Imperial Barge

A high point of land jutting out into the sea.

A long, curling wave rolling in to shore.

A band worn around the head.
A busy port on the Bay of Naples, one of the main harbours for ships trading with Rome.
Rome’s harbour town at the mouth of the river Tiber.
The ancient Arpinum, a hill town south-east of Rome, known as the birthplace of the orator Cicero.
The mountain chain that runs down the length of Italy.

Writing material made from strips of a reed that grows along the Nile, pressed into sheets.
Greek was spoken across the eastern Mediterranean, and educated Romans read and wrote it as well as Latin.
Men trained to fight in the arena for public shows. Many were prisoners of war, slaves or condemned criminals, and spectators often bet on the outcome.

The blessings beginning “Blessed are the poor in spirit” that open the Sermon on the Mount in Matthew’s Gospel.
In Luke’s Gospel, a wealthy chief tax collector of Jericho who climbed a tree to see Jesus pass.
A miracle told in all four Gospels, in which a great crowd is fed from a few loaves and fish.
A village in Galilee where, in John’s Gospel, Jesus turns water into wine at a wedding.
A saying of Jesus in the Gospels: foxes have holes and birds have nests, but he has nowhere to lay his head.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus get off The Augusta?
o: He persuaded the captain to land him at Ostia
He slipped over the stern at night and swam ashore
He hid down in the hold until the barge reached Rome
He paid a sentry to row him out to the lighthouse
quiz.e: Near the lighthouse at Capua he let himself into the sea while the sentry fetched a chair, and swam a long way to shore with the Robe and his gold.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus tell Vobiscus when offered the post of scrivener?
o: That he could not write well enough for letters
That he wanted the work for one week at most
That he would take it only if the pay were doubled
That he would much rather pick the melons
quiz.e: He said he preferred picking melons out in the open, with the mountain in sight; Vobiscus asked whether he was crazy.

quiz.q: How did Marcellus deal with Kaeso at their first meeting?
o: He laughed at his ranting and rebuked his rudeness
He bowed low and humbly begged him for any work
He told him straight away he was a Senator’s son
He offered to work for nothing but his bed and board
quiz.e: He grinned at Kaeso’s tirade, sat down uninvited and told him his manners didn’t belong in such a beautiful villa, and was ordered out.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus do with his basket of melons when Kaeso sent for him?
o: He carried it up to the villa as a gift for Kaeso
He tipped it into the cart waiting at the gate
He shared it out among the pickers along the row
He left it with Vobiscus to count toward his pay
quiz.e: He poured melons into the baskets of the old man, Metella and the others, ending with the oaf who had mocked him.

quiz.q: What did Antonia say gave Marcellus away as a patrician?
o: A ring with his family’s seal on his finger
The accent of a man brought up in Athens
His voice, his bearing and his soft hands
A letter she had found among his things
quiz.e: She said it was in his voice, his face and his carriage, and that his hands had never done work; the silk tunic didn’t help.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus model in clay for Antony?
o: A swimming-pool with bathers around it
Two gladiators squared up for a fight
A melon cart drawn by a stubborn donkey
The great mountain towering over Arpino
quiz.e: He worked most of the night on a pool with bathers, an old man with a long beard and a baby about to tumble in.

quiz.q: What was Kaeso’s comment when he saw Antony’s model?
o: That clay was no pastime for a real man
That the bathers looked like his workers
That a pool would cost more than it was worth
That it stood where spring floods would wreck it
quiz.e: He said the pool was in the wrong place, because the spring freshets would tear out the masonry, and must be built on higher ground.

quiz.q: What bargain did Marcellus strike over Vobiscus’ wages?
o: Vobiscus would be paid in fruit rather than coin
Marcellus took less pay so Vobiscus could have more
Vobiscus would be told it was Marcellus’ idea
Vobiscus’ pay would rise only if the harvest went well
quiz.e: Vobiscus was to get ten sesterces instead of six, Marcellus would take sixteen instead of twenty, and Vobiscus was not to know how it came about.

quiz.q: What did Marcellus read to the villagers on his last evening?
o: Jesus’ words on “the blessed life”, as Justus recalled them
A letter from Diana that he had carried since Capri
Lines of Virgil in praise of the farmers of Italy
A promise from Kaeso of better wages next year
quiz.e: He read the blessings Justus had recited for him and he had written down, beginning “Blessed are the poor in spirit”.

quiz.q: What news did Marcellus hear at the tavern in Alatri?
o: That Tiberius had died on Capri
That Diana had been given to Gaius
That his father had been exiled
That Prince Gaius had died at a banquet
quiz.e: Gaius had been taken ill at a banquet in the home of Quintus and Celia and died within the hour, probably poisoned; Marcellus also learned Lucia had married Tullus.

A feeling of guilt or unease that holds someone back from doing something.
Anxious care or concern for someone.
Done only as a duty, with little care or feeling.
Wise lawmakers, after the Athenian statesman Solon; often used jokingly of legislators.
Given over to drunkenness and wild, immoral living.
A small cave, especially one by the sea.
To seal the seams of a boat, traditionally with tarry pitch and loose fibre called tow.
A small pointed tool for piercing holes.
An official order issued by a ruler.
Like a maze: full of winding, confusing passages.
A soft, porous stone, often of volcanic origin, that is easy to cut.
An underground room or vault used for burial.
The beam or stone across the top of a doorway.
Once the two highest officials of the Roman Republic, elected every year; under the emperors the title remained a great honour.
A phrase from the satirist Juvenal for keeping the city’s poor content with free grain and public shows.
The “Sacred Way”, the main street through the Roman Forum, used by triumphal processions.
The forum built by Julius Caesar next to the old Roman Forum.
The Appian Way, Rome’s oldest great road, running south-east from the city towards Capua and the port of Brundisium.
A town on the coast between Rome and Naples, on the Appian Way.
Rome had a large Jewish community, much of it living across the Tiber from the city centre.
Antiochus IV, a Greek king of Syria who tried to stamp out Jewish worship in the second century BC, provoking the Maccabean revolt.
The Greek word for fish. Its letters begin the Greek words for “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”, and early Christians used the fish as a sign.

quiz.q: What did Julia do as soon as the news of Gaius’ death reached Capri?
o: Hurried to break it to Tiberius at his bedside
Sent for Sejanus to take charge in Rome
Ordered a grand state funeral for her son
Sent the courier straight back with a letter to Caligula
quiz.e: She forbade anyone to tell Tiberius and pushed the exhausted Centurion off the island with an urgent letter to her grandson.

quiz.q: What did the dying Tiberius agree to, with Senators at his bedside?
o: That Sejanus should rule as regent for a time
That Caligula should have the Empire
That Diana should be married to Caligula
That the Senate should choose his heir
quiz.e: Prompted by Julia, he whispered “Yes” when she asked whether Caligula was to be Emperor.

quiz.q: How did Demetrius know the melon from Arpino came from Marcellus?
o: A rough fish was scratched into its skin
Marcellus’ seal was pressed into the box
The bargeman described the man who sent it
A note in Greek was tucked under the slats
quiz.e: The crude outline of a fish, the Christians’ secret sign, told him a Christian at Arpino had sent it.

quiz.q: What had Demetrius been secretly doing at the pergola?
o: Hiding letters from Marcellus under the floor
Storing food and water for a long voyage
Braiding hemp into a long, strong rope
Teaching Diana to row in the dark grotto
quiz.e: He twisted hemp from the wharves into cord and hid a huge coil under the sea side of the pergola floor.

quiz.q: What happened as Diana climbed down the cliff?
o: Guards began hauling her up, so she let go and jumped
The rope snapped and she dropped into the waves below
She froze halfway and Demetrius climbed to fetch her
She lost her grip and slid down onto the rocks
quiz.e: Acteus and another guard started pulling the rope up; at Demetrius’ shout she leaped into the sea and he pulled her into the dory.

quiz.q: Why did Quintus say Demetrius should be dealt with before Diana was taken?
o: He knew where Marcellus was hiding in Rome
He could rouse the Christians of Rome into open revolt
He would steal her away again before any trial
He would risk his life to avenge her on the Emperor
quiz.e: Quintus warned that the Greek, sworn to protect her, would not hesitate to take revenge, perhaps leaping onto the Emperor’s chariot with a dagger.

quiz.q: What did Marcipor reveal at the old Jewish cemetery?
o: That Gallio already knew Marcellus was alive
That he himself was a Christian
That Diana had escaped and was in hiding
That the Emperor had put a price on Marcellus
quiz.e: Marcipor said he belonged to the Christians of Rome, nearly four thousand of them, and led Marcellus to their leaders’ meeting.

quiz.q: Who was speaking to the gathering in the tombs?
o: Laeto
Stephanos
The Big Fisherman
Justus
quiz.e: Marcellus recognized the deep voice of the huge, bearded man at once: it was the Big Fisherman.

The Appian Way, Rome’s oldest great road, running south-east from the city.

King of the Roman gods, whose great temple stood on the Capitoline Hill.
A central theme of Jesus’ teaching in the Gospels: God’s rule of justice and peace, already beginning and still to come.

quiz.q: Why did Diana stop Vobiscus giving the donkey some hay?
o: Demetrius was hidden underneath it
The hay was spoiled and made animals ill
It was a gift for Kaeso’s horses
She had gold coins buried in it
quiz.e: Vobiscus grew suspicious and dug into the cart, uncovering the “sick brother”, Demetrius.

quiz.q: How did Vobiscus check that Demetrius was the man Marcellus had contacted?
o: He asked to see the slave’s papers from Capri
He sent the Macedonian up to fetch Antonia
He asked what message had come, and heard of the fish
He tested him with a question put in Greek
quiz.e: Demetrius said the message was a small melon in a box with a picture of a fish, which matched what Vobiscus knew.

quiz.q: What did Antony conclude about Marcellus at dinner?
o: He had come to Arpino only to hide from the Emperor
He hoped to stir the villagers to rise against Rome
He would soon tire of the Christians and go home
He must spend his life doing good to atone to Jesus
quiz.e: Learning that Marcellus had crucified Jesus, Antony declared that the only way he could square it was to spend his life helping others.

quiz.q: Why did hiding Diana among the vineyard workers seem a good plan?
o: The legionaries would not dare to enter the fields
The soldiers had searched the villa but not the workers
Metella’s family owed a debt to Legate Gallus
The vineyard lay much too far from the highway to be seen
quiz.e: Kaeso noted that the searchers had gone through the villa but never asked among the laborers; Diana thought it might be fun.

quiz.q: How had Demetrius been wounded?
o: A sentry stabbed him at the gate of Gallio’s villa
He fell from Kaeso’s horse on the stony road
Quintus himself attacked him in a Roman street
A cavalryman’s sword cut him as he unhorsed him
quiz.e: Chased by three cavalrymen on the Via Appia, he was nicked by one while dragging him out of the saddle.

quiz.q: What alarming news did Lucia give her father?
o: Tullus had been ordered to raid the Catacombs
Tullus had been sent out to arrest Demetrius on sight
Sarpedon had already told the palace guards
Quintus had seen Marcellus in the city
quiz.e: Lucia cried that Christians there were to be killed and her husband Tullus had orders to raid the Catacombs.

quiz.q: What did Peter tell Demetrius before leaving?
o: To stay in Rome and guard Marcellus’ family
To go to Arpino and bring Diana to safety
To return to his countrymen and testify for the Christos
To tell no one how he had been brought back
quiz.e: Peter reminded him of the promise made for him: he was to go back to the Greeks and testify for the Christos who had made him whole.

quiz.q: How did Senator Gallio plan to get Demetrius away?
o: Hide him in a wine cart going to Arpino
Take him himself by carriage to an Adriatic port
Send him off with Marcellus on a fast horse
Ship him out of Ostia disguised as a common sailor
quiz.e: Gallio would ride with him to Pescara and, if need be, charter a ship as far as Brundisium so he could reach Corinth.

quiz.q: Why was this a good day to slip out of Rome unnoticed?
o: The Emperor had sailed for Capri with his guards
The city was absorbed in the coming Ludi Romani
The gates were left unguarded after a storm
The patrols had all been sent to the Catacombs
quiz.e: With the great festival to Jupiter only days away, the roads were jammed with merrymakers and no one questioned the carriage.

quiz.q: Why did Kaeso urge Marcellus to marry Diana at once?
o: So Caligula could no longer pretend concern for her
Antonia had already planned a wedding feast for that night
Her mother had written asking them to marry
The villagers expected a wedding before the grapes
quiz.e: As Marcellus was thought dead, Caligula claimed an interest in her welfare; once she was married he would have no excuse.

quiz.q: Where did the wedding take place?
o: In the atrium of the villa, with only the family
In the vineyard among the rows of ripe vines
On the village green, before all of Arpino
In the temple at Alatri, in front of a priest
quiz.e: Kaeso married them at sunset under a little arbor on the green where Marcellus used to tell his stories.

quiz.q: Why did Sarpedon go to Quintus?
o: He wanted the reward posted for news of Diana
He owed Quintus money and needed his favour
Quintus had ordered physicians to report Christians
His pride was hurt and he wished to side with Caligula
quiz.e: Wounded by Marcellus’ words, he also judged it wise to show Quintus he was on the Emperor’s side against the old Senators.

quiz.q: How did Quintus get Diana to accept the banquet invitation?
o: He threatened to arrest her mother Paula
He promised she could leave before the speeches
He hinted it might help Marcellus’ case
He said Senator Gallio had asked her to come
quiz.e: He told her the Emperor’s judgment of Marcellus might be tempered if she were gracious to him, and she agreed.

quiz.q: What happened when Marcellus handed over the Robe at his trial?
o: Caligula tore it and flung it at his feet
It was dropped twice and given to Diana
Salome claimed it as her prize in the wager
The Commander had it locked away as evidence
quiz.e: The Centurion and then a guard let it fall, and Caligula had it handed to Diana to keep “as a memento”.

quiz.q: What did Diana do after Marcellus was sentenced?
o: She begged Caligula on her knees to spare him
She fainted and was carried from the hall
She asked Gallio to go and plead with the whole Senate
She declared herself a Christian and joined him
quiz.e: She walked down from the dais to his side, said she too was a Christian and his wife, and asked to go with him.

quiz.q: What did Diana do with the Robe as they left the palace?
o: Tossed it to Marcipor, for the Big Fisherman
Wrapped it round Marcellus’ shoulders
Handed it back to Senator Gallio
Left it on the Emperor’s high table
quiz.e: At Marcellus’ whisper she slipped between the guards and threw it to old Marcipor: “For the Big Fisherman!”
